plans.unit: story-workflow (W2: the story workflow script and its scenario tests)
plans.summary: Plan for W2, 27,974 bytes, written to /Users/jmagady/dev2/vsdd-factory/rewrite/plans/step-6/story-workflow.md. It builds next/plugins/vsdd-factory/workflows/story.js whole (hand-written meta, the build-stamped prelude region, hand-written body), one edit of the prelude's relay() prompt, and about 50 scenario tests that run the shipped file in the harness, each passing a `contract` check that asserts every dispatched call's agent, method, model and effort against the roster, the agent files and the method files. All 13 required paths are walked (what is passed, what is read, what happens next) and each has a named test. Main corrections to the skeleton: standalone, the returned status is the checkpoint's, not the script's; the survey and the close are asked once more when they print nothing; a failed survey that opened a run is closed; fixes and repairs go to the story kind's implement agent; coverage comes from the adversary alone; a later review loop takes its items from the `--since` gate result and stays on the range patch; evidence is recorded again after a repair; a blocked fixer ends blocked, not failed. Starting a run needs no new file: the prompt is `/vsdd-factory:story <story-id>`, the main session calls Workflow with name `vsdd-factory:story`, and the shipped script is proven by a named call with no `script` plus a byte comparison of the platform's `scriptPath` copy. No code was run or changed under next/; the only verification done was reading the built code and running one existing universal test (the dictated no-JSON answer), which passes. The plan depends on steps 3, 4 and 5 being built first and on one change to the step 5 plan (three agents must list `fix-findings`).

plans.unit: first-run (the story-ready fixture with its loader; the first headless run of one story: E1 fixture part, E2 first run)
plans.summary:
Plan written (27,976 bytes, eight sections). I did not read the other planner's story-workflow.md; what the driver assumes of W2 is stated as an interface in section 4.

(a) Fixture. The overlay is a small manifest plus three artifact files (contract BC-1.01.001, epic E-1, story S-1.01 "add median()", kind feature, criticality low, demo false, four acceptance criteria that each name an assertable value) and an oracle script that is never copied into the project. The loader runs make_sample_repo.sh -n, the real init, sets three keys in the sample's own factory.toml (mode local, ci none, push false), copies the artifacts, then make_ready() writes the cycle, the approved brief and spec decisions (digest from digests.spec_digest after the contract is in place) and the plan closure through the stores, flushes, and post-checks. I ran this recipe against the built code in a scratch directory: flush committed, validate clean, every precondition met, and the built survey admitted S-1.01 and returned tier_override {sonnet, low} under VSDD_TEST_TIER. make_ready is the one description of a ready project: tests/unit/story_ready.py is changed to call it, as its docstring and the step 3 plan promised.

(b) Driver. `cd next && uv run --no-sync python -B tests/e2e/run.py story` creates a run directory under ~/.cache/vsdd-factory/e2e/, copies the plugin, loads the fixture, refuses to start on seven named conditions (two of them sandbox checks), starts claude -p with a table of settings each tied to a platform item, waits with its own time limit, runs twelve checks, writes report.json and prints a diagnosis with one cause and the resume line. Default tier is cheap (sonnet:low through the survey's override; expected 1 to 3 dollars, 6 to 9 agent starts); --tier roster is the switch (expected 6 to 15 dollars). Both figures are estimates.

(c) Checks read files, git and the event log only. Two things the slice cannot give from the event log are taken from the hook runner's built capture switch (VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_CAPTURE): agent starts (distinct agent_id) and per-step effort. The driver is tested with a stand-in for the claude binary and with a scripted delivery of the fixture story through the real gates, delivery and checkpoint, so every check has a passing and a failing test with no model.

Things to know before building:
- Isolation flags (--setting-sources project,local, --strict-mcp-config) are on by default but unproven with a --plugin-dir plugin; --user-settings drops them. --no-session-persistence is deliberately not passed, against packaging/tests-e2e.md.
- This machine now has Claude Code 2.1.332; the platform record was made on 2.1.331.
- Found while reading, confirmed by running in scratch: story_ready.make_project(product=<the sample directory>) as built copies the sample's .factory/factory.toml over the project's, leaving delivery.mode = "pr", state.push = true and paths.source including ".factory/**". Step 4's gate_project.py is planned on exactly that call.

D3: records are made through the stores from a small manifest, not copied as JSON files, although the spec lists them as overlay files
D4: the fixture keeps the shipped merge_strategy squash; the checks run at once on the then-unreachable commits and fail by name if one is gone
D5: the run directory is under $HOME (~/.cache/vsdd-factory/e2e/), because probes ran only there and under Claude Code's own temp tree; --dir may name any place outside a git work tree
D6: the session runs a copy of the plugin made once per run directory, so concurrent edits under next/ cannot change a run, its resume or its diagnosis

D7: the sandbox is made sure of three ways (a write test under .git/worktrees/ by the driver's own process, a scan of the settings files the session will load, --settings with sandbox off), and a miss still fails loudly at the survey's first flush
D8: isolation flags are on by default although unproven with a --plugin-dir plugin; if they stop the plugin's hooks the survey fails at its first step and the cause names --user-settings
D9: --no-session-persistence is never passed, against packaging/tests-e2e.md, because the named-workflow check reads the session's run record
D10: agent starts are counted from captured hook payloads, not the event log; agent.start lines replace the count when the lifecycle log is built
D11: effort is asserted per step from hook payloads (item 48); the model is asserted per session from modelUsage
D12: a check that cannot measure fails; an oracle outside the project is an independent proof that main holds the change
Default tier is cheap (VSDD_TEST_TIER=sonnet:low, cap 6 dollars, 45 minutes); --tier roster (cap 30 dollars, 120 minutes) is run once after cheap passes

review.verdict: The clean path holds end to end. Every hand-over from the driver's command to the merge and the checks matches on name, arguments, fields and refusal cases. I ran the fixture recipe against the built survey and it is accepted: the story is admitted, the unit is feature with AC-1 to AC-4, and the tier override comes back. One correction has to go into the step 5 build before W2 can be built (PL6-1). Four majors should be settled before the first real run: PL6-2, PL6-3, PL6-4 and PL6-7. The rest are minor. A kept round-4 session folder already answers W2's question about scriptPath and first-run's question about the session folder: the script is identical byte for byte, and workflowProgress gives each agent's model.

findings.problem: W2 D6 sends every fix and repair to the story kind's implement agent with method fix-findings. Its contract fails any call whose method is not in the agent's list, and the test `each kind is fixed by its own builder` runs every shipped [[story-kind]] row. agents.md section 3 gives technical-writer only `docs`, devops only `repo-setup` and verifier only `proofs`, and test_agent_files.py holds each agent to that list. So W2's own tests fail on the docs, chore and harness rows, and W2 section 8 tells its builder to stop. STATE next action 5 does not carry this correction into the step 5 build. In the same way, review-story-diff's rule that the test-writer owns test and coverage findings must give way to the owner the task names. Otherwise a kind with no red gate gets findings routed to a test-writer whose re-freeze fails (gates.md D16).
findings.proposed_resolution: Put both corrections in the notes of the step 5 build. First, technical-writer, devops and verifier list fix-findings, and test_agent_files.py's method table follows. fix-findings says that for a kind with no red gate the agent fixes within its own write scope. Second, review-story-diff takes each finding's owner from the task when the task names one for every category. If that is not wanted in step 5, W2 narrows `each kind is fixed by its own builder` to the feature row and records the other rows as left for A5.

findings.problem: W2 needs the fixture's factory.toml to set spikes.per_run = 0, so that a spike request ends blocked spike_limit inside step() and never reaches runSpike(). The spike-runner has no agent file on the slice. first-run sets only three keys and does not mention this one. It could not set it anyway: config.py types spikes.per_run and per_step as INT1, an integer of at least 1 (config.py lines 51 and 162-165), so config.load refuses 0. With the shipped value of 6, any step that returns needs_spike makes the run call agent() with an agent type that has no file. What happens then is W2's own open question (throw, null, or run untyped), it is unproven, and the first-run diagnosis names no cause for it.
findings.proposed_resolution: (a) The owner of config.py allows 0 for spikes.per_step and per_run, using an INT0 kind (the spec sets no minimum). The loader sets spikes.per_run = 0 as a fourth set_key, and a fixture test asserts the survey answers limits.spikes_per_run == 0. Or (b) W2 sets RUN.limits.spikes_per_run = 0 after applyLimits, with a comment naming A3, S6 and H8, and removes it when they are built. Under either, the first-run diagnosis adds the cause spike_limit. If neither is taken, add the unknown-agentType leg to the probe of PL6-4.

findings.problem: Delivery merges only when G3's covering() finds a converged verdict rebuilt from the stored step records, so the script and the tool meet only in those records. W2's scenario stubs are shaped to fit W2's own reading. verdicts.md's records cases are written by hand. The loop conformance cases compare converge() with the Python replay, not with the records the script's steps actually produce: names, loop and pass, method, agent type, the fix's gate entries, and a later loop's items. first-run's deliver_scripted stores records the way delivery_fixtures does, not the way the script does. Nothing would catch a mismatch at this seam before the real platform answers refused.
findings.proposed_resolution: W2's test_story_workflow.py gains test_script_records_rebuild_to_the_script_verdict. It runs the shipped story.js in node for these scenarios: clean; a test finding fixed by the test-writer and then the implementer; a coverage gap; a dispute ruled not_defect; the cap; a repair that adds a file (loop 2); and review_stale. It turns each returned step result into the record the step-results rule would store: agent_type from the call's agentType, the result's head, in call order. It then calls vsdd.state.verdicts.rebuild(records, subject, cap, waived, acs, changed), with changed answered from the scenario's --since stubs. It asserts that the tool's outcome, reason, passes, rounds_used, coverage_missing and chain equal the script's verdict, and that skipped is empty.

findings.problem: Neither plan makes the platform behaviour the first run depends on a gate to be checked first. (1) Do --plugin-dir hooks, workflows and bin/ load under --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config? Every round-4 run had user settings loaded, which on this machine include skipWorkflowUsageWarning. (2) Does the typed workflow command work with no skill in default mode? Item 31 was seen only in round 3, which ran in auto mode. Round 4 always entered through the typed skill probecall, and in the C30 control the model went through Skill and was refused. W2 builds no skill on item 31 alone. (3) With bare tool names allowed, can a step Read the method file under the plugin directory (outside cwd), and Edit and Write in a linked worktree? (4) Item 26: does the effort.level in a payload show the step's effort when the session's effort differs? first-run's tier_applied assumes it does. (5) What does a --max-budget-usd stop leave in the middle of a workflow? (6) Unless PL6-2 is resolved: what happens with an agentType that has no file?
findings.proposed_resolution: Make one probe round a gate in ORDER.md before E2's first run. Run one or two headless sessions on a scratch copy of the spike plugin, each started by the typed workflow command itself (no skill), with first-run's exact flags plus --effort medium. Use a one-step workflow whose low-effort step reads a file under the plugin directory, edits and writes in a linked worktree, runs plain Bash and returns. Add a second leg: a three-step workflow under --max-budget-usd 0.05. Pass means a hook log, a workflow result, empty permission_denials, and the payload's effort recorded. Expected cost is under a dollar. Record the results as platform items, and set first-run's D8 defaults from them.

findings.problem: Confirmed by running it. tests/unit/story_ready.py _install_product (lines 132-150) copies every child of the product directory, .factory/ included, then sets paths.source to every top-level name. On the sample this gives delivery.mode = pr, state.push = true and paths.source = ['.factory/**', '.gitignore/**', 'README.md/**', 'tally/**', 'tests/**', 'tools/**'], so tests/** is both a tests class and a source class. G2's gate_project.py is built on this call, and survey-2's real-gate tests and delivery's fixtures build on gate_project. Several things would then misread the sample's tests: the red gate's rule that a source-class test does not count, tests-first's source rules, and delivery row 4.
findings.proposed_resolution: Before step 4 stage A, the survey unit, which owns story_ready.py (R1), makes two changes. It skips .factory when copying a product directory, and it sets [paths] from the product's own factory.toml when the product has one (tests = ['tests/**'], source = ['tally/**', 'tools/**']). gate_project.py asserts both. first-run's later edit of story_ready.py, where the three record writers become make_ready, leaves that code as it is.

findings.problem: The kept round-4 session folder answers first-run open question 3 and W2 open question 1. The folder is ~/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-...-pr4-project/1cf1064b-.../. Its wf_*.json has the keys script, scriptPath, status, result, agentCount and workflowProgress. For a call by name, script and the file at scriptPath equal the plugin file byte for byte. workflowProgress gives each agent's agentType and full model id, and the step transcripts carry tool_use entries. W2 asks the driver to log Workflow PreToolUse and PostToolUse through a hook, but first-run builds no such hook and does not need one, because the run-record check is what item 49 prescribes. The PostToolUse input of a named call also carries script, so a 'no script' test is valid only on PreToolUse. first-run D11 says the model is seen only in modelUsage. That cannot attribute a model to a step, and the plan gives no mapping from alias to id.
findings.proposed_resolution: Record the folder's shape as a platform item. In first-run's tier_applied, take each step's model from workflowProgress, joined to the payloads by agentId, and match an alias as a segment of the id. Use modelUsage only for the main session. Model fake_claude.py and deliver_scripted on that record shape. W2 drops the request for a hook and keeps the byte check as the driver's.

findings.problem: Under the default cheap tier the override is sonnet:low, the session runs --effort low, and the clerk tier is low too. If a payload reports the session's effort (item 26 is open), every effort.level reads low whether or not the override applied. So the run meant to settle item 18 passes tier_applied on effort without testing anything. Also, the first survey clerk runs before the override is known, at the clerk tier. With any --tier other than sonnet:low, tier_applied fails on that step, and W2's `a tier override reaches every step` has to exempt it.
findings.proposed_resolution: Assert the override from the captured StructuredOutput payload of the survey clerk (config.tier_override). That settles item 18 directly. Run the session at an effort no probe tier uses (for example --effort medium). Exempt the first survey step from both tier_applied and W2's contract, and say so in both plans.

findings.problem: W2 D11 adds to relay(): 'If the call is moved to the background, run the same command again', for every relayed command. probes-4-apply-C2-3, which STATE sends into the step 5 build, limits that sentence to job commands (story deliver): survey and checkpoint return directly, and a moved call of theirs is waited for. Being safe to repeat one after another is not the same as being safe to run beside a copy still running. Built as planned, the clerk file and the relay prompt disagree again, which is the fault C2-1 was about.
findings.proposed_resolution: Use one text in both relay() and the clerk file: 'If a vsdd story deliver call is moved to the background, run the same command again: it re-attaches to its job. A moved call of any other command: wait for it, as the notice says.' W2's clerk-prompt test checks that text.

findings.problem: W2 D4 says the built 'could not build the story unit' path keeps the lock and sets run_id. As built (survey.py lines 151-164), that path releases the lock and empties run_id (S3R-survey-C1-1), and survey-2's re-measure failure does the same. The case that is really left is different: a lock release that itself fails leaves the lock held with run_id empty. W2 cannot close that, and does not say so.
findings.proposed_resolution: Restate D4 against the code and keep the branch and its test as a defence. Name the release-fault case as the survey's to recover from: the next survey can take the run once the lock is stale, and the driver releases it through first-run refusal 7 (lock release --force).

findings.problem: W2 takes a later loop's items from the --since green result's changed_files. The schema leaves that field optional, and the step-results rule checks only gate, subject, sha and passed. A copy that drops the list therefore passes every check, and an empty item list lets the script's loop converge on nothing while the tool names files. W2's table also does not say that the test-writer's green command in a later loop carries --since <from>.
findings.proposed_resolution: W2 reads a --since entry without a changed_files array as an unusable result: the step failed, with a summary that names the field. W2 gives the test-writer the --since green command in a later loop, with one scenario test for each of these two points. gates.md may make changed_files and test_output required on a green result.

findings.problem: holdout_wall measures nothing on this fixture. The overlay has no .factory/holdout, and H2's read walls are not on the slice. Either the check passes because there is nothing to read, or, with a holdout file added, it fails for a rule the slice does not enforce.
findings.proposed_resolution: Keep the transcript reader. Report holdout_wall as not applicable (no holdout in the overlay, H2 not built) and leave it out of ok. Make it a pass condition when E2 widens with a holdout overlay and H2.

findings.problem: ORDER-4 section 7 says the script does not record evidence again after a repair, so a demo: true story is refused at the demo row. But gates.md D14's demo rule is a file check plus green covering the head, so the old recording passes at the new head and the story would merge with a demo older than the repair. W2 D9 records again, which is right either way. Not on the slice's path.
findings.proposed_resolution: The integrator strikes ORDER-4's sentence in favour of W2 D9. G2, when widened, records the commit each recording was made at and refuses a recording older than the head.

findings.problem: The gates and delivery row 6 need a clean story worktree, and M3 tells builders to commit everything. The sample's .gitignore does not cover .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/ or .mypy_cache/. A builder that runs pytest or ruff in the worktree either fails its gate on dirt or commits the cache. Committing the cache then fails integration_holds_change on a story that was delivered.
findings.proposed_resolution: first-run adds the three caches to tests/e2e/sample-project/.gitignore, beside its README and factory.toml edits, and test_sample_commands_run_offline_and_leave_nothing covers the file.

findings.problem: Section 3.7 makes a resume the person's re-run, but open question 4 says the driver treats any subtype other than success as a failed attempt and resumes. If resuming is automatic, nothing bounds the number of attempts. --max-budget-usd caps one session only, so total spend across attempts is unbounded.
findings.proposed_resolution: State that the driver never starts an attempt by itself. report.json sums cost over all attempts, and the driver refuses an attempt (exit 2) when recorded spend plus the next cap would exceed a total for the tier or --budget.

findings.problem: Some scenario tests would pass with the script wrong. No test covers a reviewer whose reviewed_sha is not the head ending failed with no_result. None checks that a later loop's fix steps and the test-writer's green command carry --since. The default step stub never returns a green result shaped like a real --since result (changed_files and range patch) unless a test overrides it. And the contract's model and effort assertion has to exempt the first survey call under an override.
findings.proposed_resolution: Add two tests: `a reviewer on another commit ends failed` and `a later loop fixes close with --since`. Make the default green stub for a --since closing return changed_files and a range diff_patch built from the scenario's files. Exempt the survey step in the tier assertion, as PL6-6 says.

findings.problem: For a story delivered within one run, the checkpoint writes only the review and deliver stage entries and then drops the evidence, and the squash merge deletes the branch. Only the local step records and unreachable loose objects, read at once after the session, show that the tests came first. A clone, or the same machine later on, cannot show it.
findings.proposed_resolution: This is first-run's question for the person, extending STATE waiting item 6. Until it is answered, run as planned. If the answer is to keep a record, survey-2's assess writes the tests and implement entries for a delivered story from the run's passing red and green step entries, which needs no evidence.
